data.title: European shares slip on AI slowdown calls and inflation concerns
data.description:
Key points:
  • Tech among top decliners after AI slowdown call; software stocks rally
  • Oil prices surge more than 2%
  • GSK gains after positive trial results for two lung cancer drugs

By Sudeshna Ghoshal and Ragini Mathur

European shares fell on Monday as technology stocks came under pressure after leaders of top AI companies pushed for a slower pace of development, while another surge in oil prices and global bond yields dampened broader risk appetite.

The pan-European STOXX 600 was down 0.5% at 635.99 points. Most regional markets declined, though London's CURRENCYCOM:UK100 and Zurich's indexes rose 0.4% and 0.8%, respectively.

Technology stocks (.SX8P) were among the biggest losers, down 2.1%, as AI-linked shares slid globally. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on Saturday for companies to slow advances in AI model capabilities over misuse concerns, a view supported by xAI's Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.

France-based chipmaker Soitec was the STOXX 600's top decliner, falling 12.5%.

Software stocks, however, gained. Octave Intelligence , Capgemini , Sage and Relx rose between 5% and 7.5%.

"These stocks were victims of the SAASpocalypse, on fears AI would wipe out their businesses," said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG.

"Those fears were overdone, but if the AI giants do put their foot on the brake, then the outlook for revenues for Sage, RELX and their SAAS brethren globally becomes much brighter, even if it only delays a longer-term loss of business."

European miners (.SXPP) fell 2.5%, with miners of both base and precious metals declining as they tracked weakness in commodity prices.

Healthcare stocks (.SXDP) bucked the broader trend to rise 2.7%. GSK gained 4.7% after reporting positive trial results for two lung cancer drugs, adding to the sector's momentum.

Energy stocks (.SXEP) were off 0.8%, though crude prices jumped 2% after fresh strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure and attacks on ships in the Middle East heightened supply concerns.

The recent oil spike has brought inflation worries up front, reinforcing expectations that central banks worldwide could increase interest rates this year. European economies are particularly vulnerable to surging oil prices as they rely heavily on imports.

ECB policymakers warned on Monday that euro zone inflation could exceed already high forecasts, while traders now price in at least one more 25-basis-point ECB increase by year-end after last week's rate hike.

The developments sent government bond yields surging, with the 10-year bund (DE10YT=RR), considered the region's benchmark, at its highest since mid-2009. Meanwhile, U.S. benchmark 10-year Treasury yields rose to the key psychological level of 5%.

This week, the U.S. Federal Reserve is widely expected to hike its main lending rate by at least 25 basis points — in contrast to a split chance between a hike and a pause seen just a week ago.

Elsewhere, Sweden's centre-left opposition looked most likely to take power on Monday after a tight election that reduced the far-right's influence.

data.title: Wheat Futures Move Lower on Russia-Ukraine News — Market Talk
data.description: Wheat futures turn lower after President Trump said on Truth Social that Ukraine and Russia agreed to stop strikes on each other's energy targets. Attacks on energy infrastructure have contributed to multiyear highs for diesel prices, while strikes on shipping in the Black Sea did the same for wheat. "Managed money length appears to be interpreting this renewed pressure from the U.S. as potentially leading to de-escalation regarding commodity flow through the Black Sea, but only time will tell if this actually translates to an improvement on the ground instead of just a headline," Mike Castle of StoneX says in a note. Wheat is down 0.6% on CBOT.(anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

data.title: KEO Capital Announces Strategic Partnership with Mastercard to Expand Cross-Border Card Program
data.description:
KEO Capital AB (publ) (“KEO Capital” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq Stockholm: KEOC) is pleased to announce a strategic partnership with Mastercard (NYSE: MA), under which Keo Capital will be granted the ability to issue Mastercard-branded cards as part of its cross-border program.

The partnership marks a significant milestone for Keo Capital, aligning the company with a Global payment leader whose network spans more than 200 countries and territories and processed over USD 10 trillion in gross dollar volume in 2025. Through this collaboration, KEO Capital will leverage Mastercard’s global infrastructure and acceptance network to substantially broaden the geographic reach of international markets for its clients and program participants.

Under the terms of the agreement, the partnership has an initial term of 5 years, providing long-term stability and a clear framework for continued growth. The agreement includes U.S. Dollar as authorized currency for all Corporate Purchasing Cards & Travel and Expenses Cards issued under the program, enabling greater flexibility for cross-border transactions and international commerce.

The partnership complements Keo Capital's existing collaborations and further validates the strength and market fit of the Company's cross-border offering. Partnering with a payment provider of Mastercard's scale to expand the program demonstrates broader interest in the product among global partners and supports KEO Capital's expansion in international markets.

“This partnership complements our existing collaborations and gives the program significantly greater reach, including into new markets. Partnering with a company of Mastercard’s global scale is a strong validation of what we’ve built, and we are excited to bring even greater value and flexibility to our cross-border program participants over the course of this five-year agreement,” commented Roberto Marchiori, COO of KEO Capital.

Contacts

Pablo Ribas, CEO | Miles Molyneaux, CFO | Roberto Marchiori, COO | Jakob Sintring, Head of IR

Phone: +46 8 611 05 11, E-mail: IR@keocapital.com

About KEO Capital

KEO Capital AB (publ) is a listed technology-driven financial solutions provider focused on improving liquidity, security, transparency, and efficiency in B2B supply chain financing and corporate travel and expense management. KEO Capital operates a unified digital ecosystem that enables buyers and suppliers to interact through complementary solutions designed to address the full spectrum of corporate payables. KEO Capital’s energy activities, including its indirect equity interest in PetroUrdaneta (24 percent, to be increased to 40 percent under a binding agreement), are held through KEO Energy and are intended to be separated from the Company, following which KEO Capital will focus exclusively on its fintech business. The shares are listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (KEOC). For more information, please visit the Company’s website https://keocapital.com/.

This information is information that KEO Capital is obliged to make public pursuant to the EU Market Abuse Regulation. The information was submitted for publication, through the agency of the contact persons set out above, at 2026-09-14 18:46 CEST.

data.title: Basis bids mostly steady-lower as Midwest harvest nears
data.description:
Spot cash basis bids for corn and soybeans were steady to lower at most elevators and processing plants around the U.S. Midwest on Monday as recent farmer sales have boosted supplies and as buyers await the upcoming harvest.

  • Premiums offered to farmers for near-term deliveries expired at several elevators and processors. Spot basis bids fell by up to 30 cents a bushel at ethanol plants and soy crush plants.

  • In one exception to the overall weak tone in basis, a soy crusher in Council Bluffs, Iowa, raised its spot bid by 25 cents a bushel for supplies delivered by the end of this week, reflecting an 80-cent premium over supplies delivered later in the month.

  • Harvesting is due to begin ramping up in the Midwest in the coming weeks as crop maturity is ahead of the normal pace in many areas. The U.S. Department of Agriculture is due to update its crop progress and conditions estimates later on Monday.

  • CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were up 11-1/2 cents near midday on Monday at $13.08 a bushel, while December corn (CZ26) was 2-1/2 cents higher at $5.32-3/4 a bushel.

data.title: Waymo Launches Robotaxis in Las Vegas
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Waymo has added Las Vegas to its repertoire of cities where its self-driving cabs are available.

The robotaxi company, which is owned by Alphabet, said Monday it is now providing fully autonomous rides to the public in the popular Nevada city.

Waymo plans to give increasing access to more riders in Clark County, Nev., as it works toward opening its services to everyone.

Earlier this month, Waymo launched driverless rides in Denver, San Diego and Tampa, Fla.

Competitors including Tesla and Amazon's Zoox have also been ramping up the number of cities where they operate.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: TransAlta Ordered by U.S. Government to Keep Washington Coal Unit Online for 90 More Days
data.description:
By Adriano Marchese

TransAlta has received another order from the U.S. Department of Energy to keep Washington state's last coal-fired power plant operational for an additional 90 days.

The Calgary, Alberta-based power generator said Monday that its subsidiary TransAlta Centralia Generation received the order from federal regulators mandating that Unit 2 of its Centralia Generating Station remain available to support the grid.

The station is now ordered to remain available for operations until Dec. 12.

The power station was earmarked for closure at the end of 2025 as part of a shift toward cleaner sources to generate power but has received three other requests to keep the plant operational. The company had already retired Unit 1 at the end of 2020 as part of a state mandated two-phase closure of the coal-fired plant.

TransAlta said Monday that it will continue to comply with the directive while coordinating with state and federal officials.

Write to Adriano Marchese at adriano.marchese@wsj.com

data.title: AI CEOs' Call for Regulation Could Benefit Biggest Players — Market Talk
data.description: Investors in the AI trade shouldn't get hysterical about top AI company leaders calling for a development slowdown and more guardrails for the industry, Melius Research analysts say in a research note. The top AI CEOs have been endorsing a slowdown for several years already, and most AI leaders have thought the space was bound for regulation anyway, they say. If anything, Anthropic and OpenAI are the companies that can benefit most from a regulatory framework that creates a predictable playing field for the most well-resourced and advanced companies, the analysts say. "It can be morally right and advantageous at the same time," they say. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

data.title: Charles Schwab to Bring Anthropic's Claude to Registered Investment Advisors
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Charles Schwab is partnering with Anthropic to bring Claude to registered investment advisors.

The brokerage on Monday said its Schwab Advisor Services business will provide Anthropic's Claude for Financial Advisors offering to more than 16,000 independent RIAs.

Schwab said its unit is the first RIA custodian that is integrated with Claude for Financial Advisors, an Anthropic offering that assists advisors with tasks like financial plan updates, analytics, and client follow-up.

"Independent advisors have always succeeded on the strength of their relationships, and relationships are built on advice, service and client experiences that stand apart," Schwab Advisor Services head Jon Beatty said. "AI is exponentially powering the ability of advisors to stand apart in this way, even more so if it is integrated with the proprietary workflows and tech stacks advisors have already built."

Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com

data.title: Trump Says AI Doesn't Need More Guardrails Despite Industry Warnings — WSJ
data.description:
By Brian Schwartz

President Trump pushed back on the need for tighter federal regulations linked to artificial intelligence, even as industry leaders sound urgent warnings about potential dangers from their own technology.

"The only control or 'guardrails' that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!" Trump wrote on Truth Social on Monday. "There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China."

The post is the latest instance of Trump publicly playing down the need for extensive oversight onto AI. His position on additional federal oversight of the AI comes as executives, including his ally Elon Musk, call to slow down advancements of the booming technology out of concern of the risks it could create, in what has become a rapidly escalating crisis for the industry.

Trump's position on AI and data centers contrasts with how many voters feel about the issue heading into the midterms. A March Gallup poll showed that nearly half of those surveyed "strongly oppose" the construction of local AI data centers. And the opposition isn't just coming from Democrats-just under 40% of Republicans polled by Gallup are strongly against the creation of data centers. The outcry has become a mounting political liability for Republicans and some Democrats ahead of the election in November.

"We can put up guardrails, and we can do this and that, but I think you have a lot of negative forces that are bringing it up," Trump told reporters Sunday while traveling in Ireland. "And they're bringing up things that won't happen." Trump has also said he uses AI but declined to provide further details.

Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei has been among the lead voices calling to slow down AI's development. In a post to his personal blog, Amodei called for the AI industry to pace development of cutting-edge tools, suggesting new measures including more global coordination among democratic countries and the introduction of embedded third-party safety evaluators.

"I believe that if slowing down bought us even an extra year or two before models reach critical levels of capability, and we used that time to advance alignment, we could greatly reduce the risk that something goes seriously wrong," he wrote.

Anthropic and the Trump administration have been clashing for months. Anthropic sued the administration after the Pentagon marked the company as a supply chain risk, and argued the Pentagon illegally retaliated against the company for its standing on artificial intelligence safety. A federal judge recently ruled in favor of Anthropic and found the administration's actions were unlawful.

An Anthropic researcher, Jacob Coxon, recently said he was quitting the artificial-intelligence industry over fears that the lab and its competitors are racing to build systems they won't be able to control, a sign of mounting safety concerns within top AI companies.

Coxon, who specializes in training new AI models by having them consume vast amounts of data, said he doesn't want to participate in an industrywide rush to build AI systems that can improve themselves, worried such systems could spiral out of control and destroy humanity.

Other tech companies have signaled a need for caution. Microsoft published a provisional code of conduct that it aims to apply when training new AI models. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman also warned that the dizzying pace of progress could go "very badly" and that humans could lose "control of the future to AI."

"We welcome a federal framework that sets consistent safety requirements for frontier AI," Altman said in a post on X. "No amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness."

Write to Brian Schwartz at brian.schwartz@wsj.com

data.title: KPS CAPITAL PARTNERS TO SELL METRA TO GRUPA KĘTY S.A. FOR €645 MILLION
data.description:
NEW YORK, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- KPS Capital Partners, LP ("KPS") announced today that it has signed a definitive agreement to sell its portfolio company Metra (the "Company") to Grupa Kęty S.A. ("Grupa Kęty", WSE: KTY), a Warsaw-listed Polish industrial group operating in the global aluminum extrusion, architectural and sun protection systems, and flexible packaging industries, for €645 million.  Completion of the transaction is expected in the first quarter of 2027 and is subject to customary closing conditions and approvals.

Metra is a leading global, vertically integrated manufacturer of extruded aluminum profiles and related value-added services, including painting, oxidation, machining, welding and assembly.  The Company offers a full range of extruded aluminum profiles, which are used primarily in rail, industrial and building & construction end-markets across Europe and North America.  Metra is headquartered in Rodengo Saiano, Italy, and has nine global manufacturing facilities and approximately 1,400 employees.

KPS acquired Metra in July 2021.  KPS and Metra's management team successfully transformed the Company into a leading, global aluminum extrusion solutions provider by capitalizing on its extensive technical, operational and value-added services capabilities. Metra's management team successfully executed an aggressive organic and inorganic growth strategy to expand in high-growth geographies and end-markets including rail, energy distribution and building & construction. Under KPS' ownership, the Company made significant investments in the Metra platform, including completing five highly synergistic add-on acquisitions, investing in new press and value-added services capabilities and manufacturing capacity expansions, and instilling a culture of operational excellence throughout the Company's global operations.

Pierre de Villeméjane, a Partner and Co-Head of KPS Mid-Cap Investments, said, "The success of our investment in Metra exemplifies KPS' investment strategy of seeing value where others do not, buying right and making businesses better, across economic and business cycles, geographies and industries.  We are proud of Metra's extraordinary transformation under our ownership.  Metra demonstrates our ability to partner with world-class management teams to build industry-leading manufacturing companies on a global basis.  We view the Company's success as a direct result of KPS' commitment to, and investment in, Metra's operations, strategic growth initiatives and its people."

Mr. de Villeméjane added, "We congratulate and thank Enrico Zampedri, Metra's Chief Executive Officer, along with the Company's senior leadership team and the entire organization, for their strategic vision and tremendous execution, which resulted in the Company's significant value creation under our ownership.  Metra is well-positioned for continued growth and industry leadership under Grupa Kęty's ownership."

Enrico Zampedri added, "Our partnership with KPS was exceptional.  KPS recognized the underlying potential of Metra and actively supported the entire leadership team through a significant business transformation over the past five years.  Under KPS' ownership, Metra improved its market positioning in the extrusion sector by investing material resources in our workforce and operations, focusing on manufacturing excellence and providing world-class product quality and support to our customer base.  We thank our customers, suppliers and employees for their contributions to our success.  Metra expects to continue its positive trajectory as an integral part of Grupa Kęty.  On behalf of the entire Metra management team, we are extremely excited about Metra's future under Grupa Kęty's ownership. This combination will provide additional scale, technical depth, value-added services capabilities and a broader global footprint to allow the combined Company to better serve our customers.  We are eager to embark on our next chapter of growth with the Grupa Kęty team."

Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP served as legal counsel and BofA Securities and Barclays Capital Inc. served as financial advisors to KPS and Metra.

About MetraMetra is a global, vertically integrated manufacturer of extruded aluminum profiles and related value-added services, including painting, oxidation, machining, welding and assembly.  The Company offers a full range of extruded aluminum profiles, which are used primarily in rail, industrial and building & construction end-markets across Europe and North America.  Metra is headquartered in Rodengo Saiano, Italy, with nine global manufacturing facilities and has approximately 1,400 employees.  More information can be found at www.metra.eu/en.

About KPS Capital Partners, LPKPS, through its affiliated management entities, is the manager of the KPS Special Situations Funds, a family of investment funds with approximately $19.1 billion of assets under management (as of June 30, 2026).  For over three decades, the Partners of KPS have worked vigorously to realize significant capital appreciation by making controlling equity investments in manufacturing and industrial companies across a diverse array of industries, including basic materials, branded consumer, healthcare and luxury products, automotive parts, capital equipment and general manufacturing.  KPS seeks to create value for its investors by working constructively with talented management teams to make businesses better, and generate investment returns by structurally improving the strategic position, competitiveness and profitability of its portfolio companies, rather than primarily relying on financial leverage.  The KPS Funds' portfolio companies currently generate aggregate annual revenues of approximately $26.1 billion, operate 277 manufacturing facilities in 25 countries, and have approximately 62,000 employees, directly and through joint ventures worldwide (as of June 30, 2026).  The KPS investment strategy and portfolio companies are described in detail at www.kpsfund.com.

KPS Mid-Cap targets the same type of investment opportunities and utilizes the same investment strategy that KPS' flagship funds have employed for over three decades.  KPS Mid-Cap aims to leverage and benefit from KPS' global platform, reputation, track record, infrastructure, best practices, knowledge and experience.  The KPS Mid-Cap investment team is managed by Partners Pierre de Villeméjane and Ryan Harrison, who lead a team of experienced and talented professionals.

About Grupa Kęty S.A.Headquartered in Kety, Poland, Grupa Kęty is a publicly-listed leading producer of aluminum profiles and components across a variety of applications like facade systems, doors and windows, internal structures, external aluminum roller shutters, and roller gates for construction markets. It also produces and sells pergolas, external blinds, awnings, reflex screens, and sunbreakers in addition to printed flexible packaging and BOPP films for food manufacturers and other sectors. Founded in 1953, Grupa Kęty was formerly known as Zaklady Metali Lekkich 'Kęty' and changed its name to Grupa Kęty S.A. in 2000.  Further information is available at https://grupakety.com.

data.title: Orlen sees no immediate supply disruptions as Saudi oil deliveries set to drop
data.description:
Poland's Orlen said on Monday it saw no immediate supply disruptions even as shipping data pointed to a steep decline in Saudi crude cargoes scheduled to move from Egypt's Sidi Kerir terminal to Poland this month.

In August, 10 tankers carrying a combined volume of 6.6 million barrels departed for Gdansk from Sidi Kerir in Egypt, LSEG data showed.

Three tankers with a total oil volume of 2.1 million barrels were set to take the route this month, including two provisional deals, data showed. Saudi Aramco supplies some 40% of the oil processed by Orlen.

"Feedstock deliveries to group refineries are proceeding without disruption. The company consistently diversifies its supply sources and expands its own upstream operations," Orlen's press office said, without addressing directly the drop in Sidi Kerir's deliveries.

State-controlled Orlen is the largest listed energy company in Central and Eastern Europe, and one of the largest buyers of Saudi crude in Europe.

MarineTraffic vessel-tracking data showed crude oil tankers from the U.S., Algeria and Norway heading to Gdansk, which feeds Orlen refineries in the same city and the group's biggest plant in Plock.

Together the refineries have a combined capacity of 486,000 barrels per day. Saudi Aramco holds a minority stake in the Gdansk refinery, while 70% is controlled by Orlen.

Saudi Arabia has temporarily shut the East-West Pipeline following a drone attack last week, disrupting a route that allows the kingdom to bypass the Strait of Hormuz and transport crude to the Red Sea export terminal of Yanbu.

Part of that crude is then shipped through Egypt's SUMED pipeline to the Mediterranean terminal of Sidi Kerir for onward exports to Europe, including Poland.

With the East-West Pipeline out of service, Yanbu will have to rely on storage inventories, which three industry sources estimate could sustain exports for only five to seven days.

data.title: Mikkeller and iGulu Bring "The Beer That Kickstarted It All" Back to Homebrewing on Kickstarter
data.description:
A new collaboration brings Mikkeller's official Beer Geek Breakfast recipe into a guided homebrewing experience with iGulu

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire-PRWeb/ -- Danish craft beer brand Mikkeller and smart homebrewing brand iGulu today announced the Mikkeller x iGulu Beer Geek Breakfast Ingredient Kit, bringing one of Mikkeller's most iconic beers into the homes of a new generation of beer enthusiasts.

Developed specifically for the iGulu smart brewing system, the collaboration gives beer lovers the opportunity not only to enjoy Beer Geek Breakfast, but also to take part in brewing it themselves.

From a Copenhagen Kitchen to the World and Back Home

Before Mikkeller became a name recognized by beer lovers around the world, its story began with homebrewing experiments in a small Copenhagen kitchen.

Mikkel Bjergsø spent years experimenting with malt, hops, and yeast, continuously brewing, tasting, and refining recipes. One simple but unconventional idea - adding French press coffee to an oatmeal stout - eventually became Beer Geek Breakfast.

With its bold coffee character and rich, silky body, Beer Geek Breakfast quickly gained international recognition. It was voted the No. 1 stout on RateBeer and became Mikkeller's major breakthrough on the international beer scene. Mikkeller later called Beer Geek Breakfast "the beer that kickstarted it all."

Now, the beer that began as a homebrewing experiment is coming home again.

Translating an Iconic Beer into a Homebrewing Experience

The Mikkeller x iGulu collaboration goes beyond placing two names on a package.

Mikkeller brings the recipe heritage and distinctive brewing character of Beer Geek Breakfast. iGulu translates that foundation into a complete homebrewing experience through a dedicated ingredient kit, guided brewing program, and controlled fermentation system.

The collaboration preserves the beer's defining profile: freshly brewed coffee, dark chocolate, and roasted malt over a smooth oat-led body. The finished beer is expected to reach 7.5-8% ABV.

How iGulu Brings the Recipe Home

A recipe determines what goes into a beer, but fermentation shapes what comes out. Beer Geek Breakfast's body, coffee expression, roasted character, and overall balance all depend on precise control of temperature, pressure, and timing.

That is where iGulu makes the difference. Users scan the RFID recipe card included in the kit, and the brewer recognizes the recipe and loads its recommended fermentation program. iGulu then automatically manages key conditions throughout each stage, including temperature and pressure, reducing the need for constant manual monitoring and adjustment.

This controlled process makes a complex stout more approachable and repeatable at home while preserving the character intended by the collaboration. The complete brewing and fermentation process takes approximately 14 days, and each kit produces around one gallon of finished beer.

Kickstarter Early Access

On September 22, the Mikkeller x iGulu Beer Geek Breakfast Ingredient Kit will make its debut through the iGulu Kickstarter campaign. Early-bird backers will receive special launch pricing and priority access, making them among the first to brew and enjoy fresh Beer Geek Breakfast at home with iGulu F2.

The kit is expected to begin shipping in Q1 2027. Final fulfillment details will be confirmed on the Kickstarter campaign page and shared with backers through campaign updates.

The ingredient kit is compatible with the iGulu S1, S1 NEO, F1, F1 PRO, and F2 brewing systems. It is also planned to remain available after the Kickstarter campaign.

Readers can learn more on the Mikkeller x iGulu product page.

Born in a Copenhagen kitchen and enjoyed in glasses around the world, Beer Geek Breakfast is now bringing its signature fresh flavor experience into homes everywhere.

This time, it is more than a beer. It is a brewing experience.
